thread:
kyle: Quick sync from PM: Sales has three customers asking for region-only routing (no remote fallbacks). We need a product decision: do we offer a priced "SoftAffinity" SKU (best-effort locality) and a "HardIsolation" SKU (strict affinity with reserved capacity), or reject no-fallback for now? I sketched pilot gating + measurable launch criteria below. feedback please.

priya: infra reality check: we cannot guarantee hard isolation without per-region reserved GPU pools + egress commitments. Cross-region KV replication will add write latency and $$$. For any "no_fallback" contract we need a minimum monthly qps reservation and a capacity sizing pass.

leo: ops perspective: we must define fail-open vs fail-closed behavior. If a region is degraded, do we block traffic (fail-closed) or allow cross-region (fail-open)? My recommendation: default fail-open for availability, opt-in fail-closed only for HardIsolation with an SLA and runbook. Also need an evacuation window and explicit migration coordinator during cutovers.

kyle: Pilot plan (proposal):
- scope: 3 pilot customers (us-east, eu-west, ap-south)
- duration: 6 weeks per customer (overlap allowed)
- mode: SoftAffinity by default, optional HardIsolation gate if customer signs reservation
- rollout: manual cutover -> automated canary -> beta self-serve
- observability: per-route P95, cost/tokens, and tenant error-blast metrics

measurable launch criteria (must be met during pilot):
- Local latency: P95 generation <= 120ms for 90% of region-local traffic
- Allowed fallback latency: cross-region P95 <= 250ms when fallback occurs
- Isolation safety: single-tenant fault injection -> other tenants error-rate delta <= 0.5%
- Autoscaling: survive 3x baseline QPS during ramp tests without OOMs or evictions
- Cost delta: per-customer token cost increase <= 25% vs baseline (or documented tradeoffs)
- Security: KMS + audit log streaming validated end-to-end
- Observability: route-level dashboards + alerts in Console
- Rollback: routing policy rollback tested (manual + automated)

priya: infra checklist for pilot (short): dedicated pool sizing, region tags in control plane, egress billing buckets, KV-replication plan, KMS creds for private deployments, SLA clause draft for reserved qps. I'll produce numbers after sizing run.

leo: runbook must cover:
- degrade ladder (what to do at 70%/85%/95% util)
- alert thresholds and paging rules
- evacuation steps (how to move tenants with minimal token loss)
- postmortem criteria if fallback used

kyle: product idea: two SKUs to surface to sales:
- SoftAffinity (lower cost): best-effort locality, automatic fallbacks, no reservation required
- HardIsolation (premium): strict region routing, no cross-region fallbacks, requires reserved capacity and 30d minimum commit

leo: require an opt-in flag in routing policy, example DSL snippet:
```
route_policy:
  - match: tenant.meta.pref_region == "ap-south"
    action: hard_isolate   # no fallback allowed
    reserve_qps: 500
  - match: tenant.meta.pref_region == "eu-west"
    action: prefer_local   # allow fallback
    fallback_policy: remote_allow
```

priya: pricing thought: HardIsolation should carry a >30% premium to cover idle reserve cost + replication overhead. Also surface egress tiers per region.

kyle: decision required by Tue EOD so Sales can respond to customers. Questions we need answered: Do we accept "no-fallback" pilot requests (with reservation)? Do we push HardIsolation GA timeline to include legal SLA and reserved billing?

ops-bot: reminder: add RFC to Platform board, tag `onramp` and `geo-affinity`. RFC due date set to 2026-07-12.

priya: :thumbsup: I'll post sizing numbers by Monday and mark blockers.

leo: :eyes: I'll draft the evacuation + degrade playbook and post to #eng-oncall tomorrow.

kyle: thanks all. final leaning: allow pilot-level no-fallback only with explicit reservation and Ops-SRE signoff. Keeps availability risk manageable. If no objections I'll finalize and send to Sales.
